newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oil chief calls rebel bombings "stupid".
newsitem.headline: Colombia oil chief calls rebel bombings "stupid".

text.p: The head of Colombia's state-run oil company branded leftist rebels "stupid" for their campaign of attacks on key oil infrastructure, in a newspaper interview Wednesday.
Antonio Urdinola added that the government's Council of Ministers would meet Friday to analyze the repeated bombings of the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, the second largest in the country.

"We don't know what the reason is behind this completely stupid campaign by the National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas," Urdinola told the leading El Tiempo newspaper. "The reasons are political not economic."
The pipeline, which has a maximum capacity to pump about 250,000 barrels per day, has been blown up 45 times this year -- the same number of times as in the whole of 1996.

It has been out of action for one week since a rebel attack last Wednesday. Two more rebel dynamite attacks and a landslide ruptured the line in three places over the weekend, forcing Occidental Petroleum Corp to shut in production and declare force majeure Monday in the Cano Limon field it operates in northeast Arauca province.
A spokesman for Occidental put the total value of lost production at the field, which produces an average of about 175,000 barrels per day, at $3.3 million a day.
But he stressed that the losses were shared between the three associate partners in the field, Occidental, Shell and Ecopetrol.
Once taxes and royalties are deducted, the spokesman said the losses in real terms were "much less" than the notional $3.3 million figure.
The spokesman said repairs on the pipeline were underway but said he did not think work would be completed before Saturday.
The Cuban-inspired ELN, set up by Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specializes in attacks on oil infrastructure.
